name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -15 point partisan lean
Incumbent Troy Balderson running with a large financial advantage
Challenger Jerrad Christian raised under $85,000 with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at roughly 95%
model.rationale: The district's -15 point partisan lean, Balderson's incumbency, and his roughly 20-to-1 fundraising edge over Christian leave the challenger without a clear path. Markets price a Republican win near 95%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge or a dramatic shift in the national environment toward Democrats could put this on the board, but no such evidence exists yet.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Balderson seeks another term in a central Ohio district that leans Republican by about 15 points. He enters the general election with roughly $2 million on hand after raising over $1.7 million, while Democrat Jerrad Christian has raised under $85,000 and holds under $20,000. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters currently flag it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Balderson about a 95% chance of winning. With no polling, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money advantage, all pointing to a comfortable Republican hold. A late infusion of outside money or an unusually favorable national climate for Democrats would be the main things to watch.
